title: U.S. Senate · Alabama

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Tommy Tuberville (R) did not seek re-election. Barry Moore, the sitting U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st Congressional District, defeated Jared Hudson in the Republican primary runoff on June 16, 2026 to win the Republican nomination. Everett Wess defeated Dakarai Larriett in the Democratic primary runoff on June 16, 2026 to win the Democratic nomination.

candidates.name: Barry Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff on June 16, 2026, defeating Jared Hudson.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st Congressional District (since 2025); previously represented Alabama's 2nd District (2021–2025) and the Alabama House of Representatives, District 91 (2010–2018)

summary.text: Barry Moore is the Republican nominee for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat and a sitting U.S. Representative. A farm-raised Enterprise businessman and Army National Guard veteran, he served in the Alabama House of Representatives from 2010 to 2018 and has been in the U.S. House since 2021, serving on the Agriculture and Judiciary committees. He won the June 16, 2026 Republican primary runoff for the Senate nomination.

background.text: Born and raised on a family farm in Coffee County, Alabama, according to his official House biography.

Earned a B.S. in agricultural science from Auburn University in 1992. After high school he served six years in the Alabama National Guard and Reserves, and Ballotpedia lists service in the U.S. Army National Guard.

After college he worked in the animal pharmaceutical industry before returning to Enterprise, Alabama, to start Hopper-Moore Inc., an industrial waste hauling company that his official biography says has also been an Alabama general contractor for more than two decades.

Was recruited to run for the Alabama House of Representatives in 2010 and served District 91 for eight years (2010-2018), including as chairman of the Military and Veterans Affairs Committee and vice chair of the Small Business and Commerce Committee.
Was elected to the U.S. House for Alabama's 2nd District in 2020 and re-elected in 2022.

After the 2023 redistricting placed him and fellow Republican incumbent Jerry Carl in the same district, defeated Carl in the March 5, 2024 Republican primary (51.7% to 48.3%) and won the general election for the renumbered 1st District.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the House Agriculture Committee and the Judiciary Committee; earlier terms included Veterans' Affairs (2021-2022). He is not seeking re-election to the House.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary to a June 16 runoff and defeated Jared Hudson for the Senate nomination.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Heather, who is also his business partner, have four children and are members of Hillcrest Baptist Church in Enterprise.

priorities.text: Points to his congressional record, saying he "was rated both the most conservative member in Alabama by CPAC and the state's most effective legislator by the Center for Legislative Excellence."

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit; Livestock, Dairy and Poultry subcommittees) and the House Committee on the Judiciary (Crime and Federal Government Surveillance; Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; and Oversight subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Ranking Member, Economic Opportunity Subcommittee) in the 117th Congress (2021-2022) while representing the former 2nd District.

candidates.name: Everett Wess
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff on June 16, 2026, defeating Dakarai Larriett.
candidates.currentRole: Midfield Municipal Court Judge, Jefferson County, Alabama (8 years)

summary.text: Everett Wess is the Democratic nominee for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat. A Birmingham attorney since the early 2000s and a Midfield municipal judge, he previously worked in technology and engineering in Huntsville and has run unsuccessfully for circuit judge. His campaign website says he is running on voting rights, equal justice, affordable health care, public education and economic opportunity.

background.text: Earned a J.D. from the Birmingham School of Law, an MBA and a B.S. in computer science (minor in mathematics) from Alabama A&M University, and an associate degree in music education from Selma University, according to his campaign website.

According to his campaign website, he worked for more than a decade in Huntsville in technology, engineering and education, including supporting NASA mission operations, military and national security systems, telecommunications and financial processing platforms, and served as an adjunct instructor at Faulkner University.

Has been Managing Partner of The Wess Law Firm, P.C. since 2001, practicing primarily estate planning and criminal defense, and for ten years served on the federal Criminal Justice Act panel representing indigent defendants.

Served as a prosecutor for the City of Midfield and a public defender for the City of Irondale, and has been a Midfield Municipal Court judge in Jefferson County for eight years, according to his campaign website.

Ran in the Democratic primary for Alabama's 10th Judicial Circuit Court in 2014, losing with 42.2% of the vote, and in 2016 finished first in the Place 26 primary before losing the runoff to Michael Streety.

His campaign website lists past roles as president of the Birmingham Bar Association's Criminal Justice Section, president of the Greater Birmingham Criminal Defense Lawyers Association and chair of the Birmingham Bar Association's Law Day Program; he is State President of the Alabama New South Coalition and a member of Avondale Church of Christ in Birmingham.
Won the Democratic primary runoff for U.S. Senate on June 16, 2026, defeating Dakarai Larriett 54.6% to 45.4%.

priorities.text: Campaign platform centers on "affordable healthcare and economic opportunity," including funding for medical providers and hospitals in rural and underserved areas.
priorities.quote: Protect Alabama Jobs, Healthcare, and Tough fair justice.

priorities.text: Says he is running to advocate for voting rights, equal justice, quality public education, and economic opportunity, and to protect the rights of Alabamians in the courts.
Emphasizes "clean government" and fair courts as part of his campaign for the Senate.

positions.summary: Campaign centers on affordable healthcare, including funding for rural hospitals and medical providers in underserved areas.

candidates.researchNotes: Wess has no Ballotpedia biography beyond his current and past judicial candidacies; background and priorities here are drawn from his campaign website, which does not itemize distinct positions issue-by-issue beyond the general platform quoted above.
